source: Ouyang et al. (2026, v2) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory - MaTTS vs vanilla best-of-N
finding: Gap 1. At equal parallel scale k=5, memory-aware scaling beats plain best-of-N sampling with the same memory, and both beat no-memory best-of-N by a wide margin. Memory gain is not just repeated attempts.
numbers: WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash, parallel k=5, Best-of-5 metric: no-memory scaling 39.0 at k=1 to 42.2 at k=5 (+3.2); MaTTS 49.7 to 55.1 (+5.4); vanilla TTS with memory (no aggregation) 52.4. Sequential k=5: MaTTS 54.5 vs vanilla 51.9; no-memory sequential fluctuates 37.4-40.6.
limits: Web-navigation, one subset, single run, no CIs. Not a reasoning-only task. Compute is equal in rollouts but MaTTS adds aggregation calls. Gap 1 is only partly closed: no frontier reasoning-task test.
agent_relevance: Best-of-N without memory adds only about 3 points; memory adds about 10. Spend tokens on memory before extra attempts, but test on our own reasoning tasks.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026, v2) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory - pass@k
finding: Pass@k with memory-aware scaling keeps growing; no-memory scaling flattens. Memory raises sample efficiency, not only the ceiling.
numbers: Shopping, parallel scaling: pass@2 = 47.6 (no memory) vs 50.8 (vanilla TTS with memory) vs 51.3 (MaTTS); pass@5 = 52.4 (no memory) vs 62.1 (MaTTS).
limits: Appendix C.3, same single setting as d01.
agent_relevance: Memory and sampling are complementary: sample diversity gives contrastive signals for lessons.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026, v2) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory - judge calibration
finding: Gap 4. A coarse LLM judge (72.7 percent accurate vs ground truth) is almost as good as an oracle writer. Success rate barely moves between 90 and 70 percent simulated judge accuracy.
numbers: Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash judge accuracy vs ground truth 72.7 percent. Simulated verifier accuracy 100 down to 50 percent: SR about 52.4 at best, 47.6 at 50 percent (random). Plotted values include 51.8, 50.6, 49.4, 48.2, 49.7.
quote: the judge's accuracy does not significantly impact the performance of ReasoningBank
limits: Noise was simulated by random label flips, not realistic correlated judge errors. ReasoningBank distils strategies from successes and failures, so label noise is less damaging than for raw-trajectory stores. Xiong add-all degradation used different designs.
agent_relevance: A cheap self-judge is acceptable as a write gate if lessons are distilled as strategies; keep a verifier for raw-trajectory stores.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026, v2) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory - small open model
finding: Gap 10. Memory still helped a small 12B open model on web tasks, so there is no hard capability threshold in this setup.
numbers: WebArena-Shopping, Gemma-3-12B-Instruct: no memory 17.1, Synapse 16.0 (below baseline), AWM 21.4, ReasoningBank 24.1 (+7.0 abs); steps 13.7 baseline vs 11.8.
limits: Appendix C.4, one model, one subset. Synapse (raw trajectories) fell below baseline: weak model plus raw cases can hurt, distilled strategies did not.
agent_relevance: Capability threshold depends on memory form: distilled items help small models, raw trajectories can harm.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026, v2) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory - authorship
finding: Resolves correction 3 in critique.md: first author of ReasoningBank is Siru Ouyang (UIUC and Google Cloud AI Research). c09 'Zhao et al.' is wrong; a28 is right.

source: Fang et al. (2025) Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory - retrieval key
finding: Gap 3. On TravelPlanner, a key from extracted task keywords (AveFact) beats a raw task-description embedding for all three models on commonsense score, and both beat random retrieval. Random retrieval still beat no memory on commonsense score.
numbers: Commonsense score (higher better): GPT-4o no memory 71.93, random 74.59, Key=Query 73.38, AveFact 76.02; Claude-3.5-sonnet 63.49 / 63.99 / 64.93 / 65.76; Qwen2.5-72b 56.57 / 59.76 / 61.71 / 63.41. Hard-constraint score is mixed (GPT-4o no memory 12.88, random 6.72).
limits: Only task-description keys compared; no reasoning-trace or situation-feature key. Recurring benchmark. Gains from random cases suggest part of the effect is generic format guidance. Single run.
agent_relevance: Feature-extracted keys (CYRUS-like) beat raw embedding by 1.7 to 2.6 points, but the gap to random is small, so distilled content matters more than the index.

source: Fang et al. (2025) Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory - build granularity
finding: Abstracted procedures beat raw trajectories on ALFWorld; scripts alone are weaker. Supports abstraction on top of raw episodes.
numbers: ALFWorld test success GPT-4o: no memory 42.14, script 56.43, trajectory 74.29, proceduralization 77.86; Claude-3.5-sonnet 34.97 / 53.59 / 71.78 / 74.72; Qwen2.5-72b 41.25 / 61.88 / 69.57 / 77.19. Steps GPT-4o 23.76 to 15.01.
limits: Proceduralization combines script plus trajectory. Recurring ALFWorld task types.
agent_relevance: Keep both raw example and abstracted procedure per case, as in early CBR norm plus episode.

source: Fang et al. (2025) Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory - plateau and transfer to weaker model
finding: Gap 7 and 10. Performance rises with number of retrieved memories, plateaus, then declines when too many are retrieved. Memory built by GPT-4o was used by a weaker Qwen2.5-14B.
numbers: Figure 5b (ALFWorld, GPT-4o): rise, plateau, decline; peak k not stated in text. Transfer to Qwen2.5-14B reported as a substantial gain on TravelPlanner; exact figures only in a figure.
limits: Figures not tabulated; the 3-4 case optimum in Memento is not confirmed numerically.
agent_relevance: Shape (plateau then decline) replicated in a second setup; tune k per model and case length.

source: Fang et al. (2025) Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory - update policy
finding: Write policies compared: vanilla append, validation (keep only successful trajectories), adjustment (revise memory in place when a retrieved memory fails). All improve over task groups; numbers are only in plots.
numbers: Figure 3 plots reward gain over no memory against trajectory group index 1 to 5 (axis up to 0.7); no numbers in text.
limits: Gap 4 only partly closed. Benchmark reward is the oracle; no LLM judge tested (authors list this as a limitation).
agent_relevance: Matches the schema step 'revise or demote a lesson on failed use'.

source: Lebowitz (1987) Experiments with Incremental Concept Formation: UNIMEM, Machine Learning 2:103-138 - scope
finding: Gap 8. UNIMEM is the follow-up to IPP: domain-independent generalisation memory run on universities, Congressional votes and terrorist events. Evaluation is by inspection of the learned hierarchy and parameter sweeps, not accuracy.
numbers: University run: 150 instances, about 20 features each. Congressional votes: 100 instances, 15 votes plus about 21 other features. Terrorist events: IPP-NLP output, 1979-1980.
quote: UNIMEM is not intended to be a psychological model per se
limits: No held-out predictive accuracy anywhere in the paper. Gap 8 answer: no measured accuracy figures for UNIMEM here.
agent_relevance: Confirms K01: early dynamic-memory work was evaluated qualitatively. Do not cite accuracy.

source: Lebowitz (1987) Experiments with Incremental Concept Formation: UNIMEM, Machine Learning 2:103-138 - parameter sweep
finding: Only numeric experiment: vary percent of features needed to generalise (25, 37.5, 50) and to retain a generalisation (20, 25) on three random sequences of 100 universities. Higher retention threshold deletes more generalisations; a stricter formation threshold lowers the deletion rate.
numbers: 6 parameter pairs x 3 sequences of 100 universities (about 20 features each; about 4-5 features to retain, 5, 8, 10 to generalise). Top-level generalisations retained: 9 to 14 on average. Creation count falls only moderately as formation threshold rises.
quote: we will not present statistical analyses
limits: Qualitative plots, averaged over 3 runs; order effects said to be 'in no case striking'. Authors give no statistics.
agent_relevance: Sets observables for a lesson-promotion ablation: number created, deleted, retained.

source: Lebowitz (1987) Experiments with Incremental Concept Formation: UNIMEM, Machine Learning 2:103-138 - spurious generalisations from few instances
finding: Gap 2. Generalising from two instances can create over-specific generalisations from accidental shared features; UNIMEM repairs them by dropping unreliable features over time. IPP-MEM, which could not refine, kept or deleted whole descriptions.
numbers: Described, not counted: terrorist domain output 'more intuitively plausible' but 'bland'; flashy IPP rule (silenced pistols against Italian political figures) lost.
quote: Large numbers of features actually hindered IPP-MEM, as it had no way to refine over-generalized concepts
limits: Wrong-lesson rate NOT measured. Qualitative judgement by the author, one domain, few examples.
agent_relevance: Supports a revise-or-demote step after promotion; no measured rate. For LLM lessons we must measure it ourselves.

source: Lebowitz (1987) Experiments with Incremental Concept Formation: UNIMEM, Machine Learning 2:103-138 - fan-out design criterion
finding: Design target: a modest number (4 to 12) of sub-generalisations under each generalisation, with instances divided roughly equally among them.
limits: Design criterion, not tested against outcomes.
agent_relevance: Cap lessons per cluster; split when a cluster grows large.

source: Gao et al. (2023) HyDE: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
finding: Gap 5 (indirect). Elaborating the query into a hypothetical document before embedding raises retrieval much over the same encoder; the closest tested analogue of Kolodner cue elaboration. It is document retrieval, not episode retrieval for agents.
numbers: TREC DL19 nDCG@10: BM25 50.6, Contriever 44.5, HyDE 61.3 (fine-tuned ContrieverFT 62.1). DL20: BM25 48.0, Contriever 42.1, HyDE 57.9 (ContrieverFT 63.2). BEIR low-resource: HyDE beats Contriever everywhere; BM25 ahead only on TREC-Covid by 0.2.
limits: Not an agent-memory study; InstructGPT (text-davinci-003). No LLM study found that tests Kolodner elaboration over episode memory. Gap 5 stays open for agents.
agent_relevance: Cheap test: have the agent write the expected situation and approach before querying the case bank; compare hit rate.

source: Shen et al. (2026) EvolMem: multi-session dialogue memory benchmark
finding: Gap 9. Third-party evaluation of A-MEM (and Mem0, HippoRAG, MemoryOS) on a shared DeepSeek-V3.2 base: no memory agent beat the base model overall. A-MEM mid-ranked and very slow.
numbers: Overall: base DeepSeek-V3.2 52.18; MemoryOS 48.66; A-MEM 44.54; Mem0 42.44; HippoRAG 33.11. A-MEM learning 40.93, habituation 9.37. Time per sample: Mem0 30.17 s, A-MEM 492.60 s (16.3x Mem0).
limits: Dialogue memory, not LoCoMo, so not a replication of A-Mem's own numbers. pdftotext table was garbled; rows read by position, base row inferred as 52.18.
agent_relevance: Independent evidence that note-evolving memory does not beat plain context; supports K21 and K22.

finding: Gap 9. A-MEM run by a third party on a 385-case forgetting benchmark: 70.6 percent on cases it can handle, 56.9 percent when unsupported cases count as failures.
numbers: 219 of 310 evaluable = 70.6 percent; 219 of 385 = 56.9 percent; 75 cases N/A (no release primitive). Four primary systems 62.9-68.3 percent. Each add_note costs one LLM call, about 14 s per case.
limits: Single author, forgetting task, not recall gains. Not a replication.
agent_relevance: Memory needs delete and demote operations; a write-only note store cannot forget.

source: Search result summary (2026-11-03): independent reproduction of AWM and A-Mem
finding: Gap 9 stays open. A search found no independent reproduction of Agent Workflow Memory; third-party A-Mem numbers (d15, d16) come from different benchmarks.
numbers: AWM authors report 24.6 percent (Mind2Web) and 51.1 percent relative (WebArena) gains; no third-party reproduction found.
limits: Search snippet only; page not opened. Absence is weak evidence.
